newsitem.title: USA: Standard Financial fights investor with injunction.
newsitem.headline: Standard Financial fights investor with injunction.

text.p: Standard Financial Inc said Wednesday that a U.S. District Court granted its motion for a preliminary injunction against LaSalle/Kross Partners L.P. and its principal investors, Peter Kross and Richard Nelson, for violations of federal securities laws.

Judge James Zagel said an amended filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission by the defendants was inaccurate because it stated the partnership's primary purpose in acquiring more than five percent of Standard Financial stock was investment, according to the company.

The Court ordered that LaSalle/Kross amend its Schedule 13D and temporarily stopped the defendants from buying or selling any shares or otherwise seeking control of Standard Financial until seven days after it has filed the amended document.

The court ordered LaSalle/Kross to change its filing to reflect "its purpose to acquire control over and influence the policies of Standard Financial by electing the Partnership's own nominees to the board of directors."

"We are gratified that the Court agreed with our contention that LaSalle/Kross violated the federal securities laws by making an inaccurate filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission," said David Mackiewich, chairman and chief executive officer of Standard Financial, in a statement.
Standard Financial is a $2.4 billion asset-holding company, which offers financial services at 14 offices in Chicago. Its shares were trading up 1/2 to 20-1/2.
